en.headline: Five Guangdong yachts make first arrival under new southbound travel scheme
en.dek: The vessels from Shenzhen, Nansha and Zhuhai docked at Lantau Yacht Club on Friday after the scheme took effect, with a welcome ceremony attended by senior officials.
body: Five Guangdong-registered yachts entered Hong Kong waters on Friday as the first batch under the new southbound yacht travel scheme.

The vessels, ranging from about 13 to 38 metres and originating from Shenzhen, Nansha and Zhuhai, docked one by one at the Lantau Yacht Club in Discovery Bay around noon, welcomed by Marine Department vessels sounding their horns.

Acting Financial Secretary Michael Wong officiated at the welcome ceremony with the Secretary for Transport and Logistics and the Director of Marine. He said Hong Kong was building itself into a yacht hub and that the scheme would open a new maritime channel for residents and visitors on both sides.

The Marine Department said yacht owners can complete arrival procedures online in advance and that designated anchorages are available. The launch follows the earlier northbound scheme for Hong Kong yachts and the signing of work arrangements with Guangdong authorities.

zh.headline: 五艘廣東遊艇在「粵艇南下」新計劃下首次抵港
zh.dek: 來自深圳、南沙及珠海的遊艇周五偽晚停泊大嶼山遊艇會，高層官員出席歡迎儀式。
body: 五艘廣東籍遊艇周五成為「粵艇南下」新計劃下首批進入香港水域的遊艇。
遊艇長度約十三至三十八米，來自深圳、南沙及珠海，中午時分先後停泊大嶼山遊艇會，海事處船隻鳴笛歡迎。
署理財政司司長黃偉紙與運輸及物流局局長、海事處處長主禮歡迎儀式。他表示香港正积極建設成為遊艇中心，計劃為兩地居民及訪客開闢新的海上通道。
海事處表示，遊艇船東可提前於線上完成入境手續，並設有指定錨泊區。此計劃繼港艇北上及粵港簽署工作安排後推出。
